Portola Point, California, is a lovely town on the Pacific Coast,

north of Los Angeles. It got its name from Gaspar de Portola, a
Spanish explorer who explored the Pacific Coast in the 18th
century. When he came to southern California, several peaceful
American Indian peoples lived there. One of these was the
Chumash people. During the 19th century the Spanish and
American settlers ! took the land away from them and built
roads, towns and cities. The last members of the Chumash went
to live on a small reservation? near Portola Point.

Bill and Michelle Martin and their family arrived at Portola
Point in March. They came from Montego Bay, Florida. Bill was a
tall, handsome boy of seventeen with brown hair and blue eyes.
Basketball was his sport and he played on the Portola High team.
He loved science and wanted to become a biologist.

His sister, Michelle, was a pretty girl of sixteen, with red hair

Their father worked for an airline and in March he was

It was hard for Bill and Michelle to leave their friends at
Montego Bay, but they often sent them emails and called them.
They liked their new school, Portola High, and made friends there.

Our story begins in July, a hot, sunny month in southern
California. School was over, and Bill and Michelle were enjoying
their summer vacation in their new home.

“Well, today’s the big day!” said Bill. “July third!”

“Yeah, in two hours we’ll see Nick again!” said Michelle
happily.

“What time is his plane landing?” asked Mrs Martin, a friendly
woman of about forty.

“At a quarter past eleven,” said Bill.

“The guest room is ready for him, and I hope you have a great
vacation together,” said Mrs Martin. “It’s almost time to drive to
the airport.”

Nick Chan was one of Bill’s best friends at Montego Bay, and
he was coming to spend the month of July with the Martins. Nick
was a Chinese-American boy of seventeen and a good basketball
player. He loved animals and wanted to become a vet. !

Nick’s plane arrived on time and the three friends were
together again.

“my name is Wild Wolf and I live on the Chumash Reservation.
I am the shaman! and the Great Spirit Manito 2 speaks to me.
Yesterday’s earthquake and the other earthquakes are signs
from the Great Spirit Manito. He is very angry because Jacob

Canyon. No one must build there! If you continue, there will be

Wild Wolf looked at Jacob Richardson who was standing in
the crowd. Then he gave the microphone back to Linda, got on
his horse and rode away. The people in the crowd turned around

fifty with gray hair and blue eyes. He was rich. He had a
successful construction company and built expensive homes in
Hollywood and Los Angeles. He was now building beautiful
homes with swimming pools and big gardens in Coyote Canyon,
the ancient Chumash cemetery.

“What does that crazy old man want?” Richardson said
angrily. “I bought that land from the state of California and paid
a lot of money for it. It’s mine and I’m going to build there.
Nobody’s going to stop me! Ha! Ancient cemetery... what

nonsense!”

Independence Day

The Fourth of July, or Independence Day, is America’s birthday. This
holiday celebrates the principles of freedom, democracy and equal

opportunity for all.

The American Revolution

The first British colony in the New World was Jamestown, in
Virginia, which was started in 1607. Later, in 1620, a group of people
called the Puritans left England because of religious problems. They
arrived on the northeast coast of North America in 1620 and founded
the Plymouth Colony. In 1630 other Puritans arrived and founded
Salem and Boston. They were hard-working people. They set up
successful businesses like fishing, whaling ! and the fur? trade.

The Puritans believed in education and founded Harvard University
in 1636 in Cambridge, Massachusetts. It is America’s oldest
university.

In the 1700s there were thirteen colonies on the Atlantic coast, all
part of Great Britain. The colonists wanted to be an independent
nation with a democratic government. They did not want to pay
taxes to Great Britain.

very angry. A group of men in Boston dressed up like American
